text:
Winnipeg went eight straight games without a win this fall, and Kyle Connor kept scoring anyway. He has 13 goals in 18 games, nine power-play points and more than 21 minutes a night, and by our win-probability numbers his goals have been worth 2.28 wins, second among 506 skaters. Two of them came in the 5-4 comeback in Montreal that started the Jets' current three-game run.

Some of this will cool. He's shooting 18% against 14% last season, 13 goals on 9.8 expected (the quality of his chances). But the luck runs the other way on his assists: with him on the ice, Winnipeg has scored 7.4 fewer goals than its chances deserve. Expect fewer goals and more helpers, and roughly the same player.

The process doesn't depend on any of that. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him carrying the puck in on 66% of his entries last season and getting 6.7 chances per 60 from right in front (87th percentile). Our projection: about 46 goals.
